task_completion.description: The agent opens the ant_task.pbl file in a text editor to identify bugs.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A text editor (like gedit, nano, or VS Code) is visible showing the contents of ~/pebl/tasks/ant/ant_task.pbl.

task_completion.description: The agent modifies the script to match the Fan et al. (2002) protocol (SOA 400ms, 4 cue types, 3 flanker types, 3 blocks).
task_completion.visual_evidence: Screenshots of the text editor show changes to variables related to SOA (400), cue conditions, flanker conditions, or block counts.

task_completion.description: The agent creates a bug report file at the specified location.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A terminal command or file explorer shows the creation of ~/pebl/tasks/ant/bug_report.txt.

task_completion.description: The agent executes the command to run the PEBL task.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A terminal shows the command 'run-pebl ~/pebl/tasks/ant/ant_task.pbl' being executed.

task_completion.description: The agent enters the required subject ID 'test01' in the PEBL launcher.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The PEBL GUI window is visible with 'test01' typed into the Subject ID field.

task_completion.description: The ANT task runs successfully without crashing, showing the experiment interface.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the PEBL experiment window displaying the ANT task (e.g., fixation cross, cues, or arrows) rather than an error message.

integrity.description: The agent actually edited the file rather than just creating a new one with the correct content.
integrity.visual_evidence: The agent is seen interacting with the existing file in a text editor, showing line-by-line changes or saves.

integrity.description: The agent ran the task through the PEBL environment, not just simulating a success message in the terminal.
integrity.visual_evidence: The PEBL graphical user interface (SDL window) is visible on the screen during the task execution phase.

integrity.description: The agent used the specific subject ID 'test01' as instructed.
integrity.visual_evidence: The string 'test01' is visible in the PEBL prompt or the terminal output logs.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The standard ANT protocol by Fan et al. (2002) requires: 1. SOA (Stimulus Onset Asynchrony) between cue and target of 400ms. 2. Four cue conditions: No Cue, Center Cue, Double Cue, Spatial Cue. 3. Three flanker conditions: Congruent, Incongruent, Neutral. 4. Three test blocks. The agent must use the command 'run-pebl' and the ID 'test01'. The bug report must be saved to ~/pebl/tasks/ant/bug_report.txt.
